_about: Where the same Module 1 item lives in each region, and how ICH CTD maps onto the ASEAN ACTD. US, EU, Japan and India codes point at this app's region packs; Canada and Switzerland headings come from Health Canada's guidance on Canadian Module 1 and the Swiss Module 1 specification v1.6. A null entry means the region has no matching heading.

CH: Information for Professionals from Other Countries

items.label: Cover letter
items.note: Every region opens with a letter. Japan files it as m1/jp/cover.pdf outside the XML; India combines it with the comprehensive table of contents.

items.label: Main application form
items.note: Form FDA 356h, the EU eAF, a copy of the Japanese application form, Form CT-18 or CT-21, Canada's regulatory transaction details (the RT XML under the Regulatory Enrolment Process), and the Swiss application form.

items.label: Prescribing information for health professionals
items.note: Prescribing information, SmPC, package insert, product monograph and Fachinformation: one product, five formats.

items.label: Carton and container labels
items.note: The EU calls them mock-ups. India files labels and cartons with the prescribing information.

items.label: Risk management plan
items.note: The US asks for a REMS only when FDA decides one is needed; the EU, Japan, Canada and Switzerland expect a risk management plan with a new active substance.

items.label: Environmental assessment
items.note: The US often files a claim of categorical exclusion. Canada's guidance says to place no documents in 1.5.

items.label: Status or decisions in other countries
items.note: Agencies that rely on others' decisions ask for them up front: India for its waiver of local trials, Switzerland under Article 13 of its Therapeutic Products Act.

items.label: Paediatric plan or waiver
items.note: The US pediatric study plan and waivers, the EU PIP decision and compliance, and Switzerland's paediatric information.

items.label: Responses to the agency's questions
items.note: The US files responses as information amendments; the EU and Switzerland have a responses element; Canada calls it solicited information.

items.label: Patent information
items.note: Patent listing links to generic entry in the US (Orange Book) and Canada (patent register).

items.label: Information about the experts
items.note: The EU and Switzerland ask for the signed expert information behind the Module 2 overviews.

actd._source: ASEAN Common Technical Dossier, Organization of the Dossier (Revision 1).
targets: Part I: Table of Contents, Administrative Data and Product Information
Part II Section B: Quality Overall Summary
Part II Section C: Body of Data
Part III Section B: Nonclinical Overview
Part III Section C: Nonclinical Written and Tabulated Summaries
Part III Section D: Nonclinical Study Reports
Part IV Section B: Clinical Overview
Part IV Section C: Clinical Summary
Part IV Section D: Tabular Listing of All Clinical Studies
Part IV Section E: Clinical Study Reports
Part IV Section F: List of Key Literature References

pairs.ctd: 5.2 Tabular Listing of All Clinical Studies

notes: ACTD has four parts, not five modules: the overviews and summaries sit at the front of the part they summarise, instead of in a separate Module 2.
Parts III and IV are not required for generics and some variations; member states may waive study reports when a reference country has approved the product.
ACTD is a paper or PDF format; it has no eCTD backbone.
